_comment: Three frames each: from the entrance looking UP, which is the question
a tower asks; from somewhere on the climb; and from above the open
shaft, where the whole route reads at once.
CAMERA FRAME (L-52): every `eye` is a manifest anchor with x and z
negated. LIGHTING (L-56): key_energy 0.70, because a tower has no roof
and the bench rig is built for a subject on a backdrop.
The _over cameras stand over the shaft CENTRE at pitch -72, not in front of it: a tower has walls as tall as it is, so any oblique from outside photographs the outside.

shots.name: T_collapsed_entry
shots.caption: COLLAPSED - 2 FLOORS, 6 M, THE SHORTEST A TOWER MAY BE
shots.note: TWO HALF-FLOORS THAT TORE AT OPPOSITE ENDS, 3.0 M APART

shots.name: T_collapsed_upper
shots.caption: ON THE UPPER HALF-FLOOR, LOOKING BACK OVER THE TEAR
shots.note: 10.8 X 6.6 M - A ROOM TWICE, NOT A CLIMB

shots.name: T_collapsed_over
shots.caption: INTO THE SHAFT FROM ABOVE
shots.note: THE CLIMB HAPPENS ON THE SLAB BELOW IT - NO JUMP CROSSES OPEN SHAFT

shots.name: T_spiral_entry
shots.caption: SPIRAL - 3 FLOORS, 9 M, THE CANONICAL SQUARE HELIX
shots.note: TOWER()'S OWN INSET AND SPACING, BUILT AS CANTILEVERED SLABS

shots.name: T_spiral_climb
shots.caption: PART WAY UP, WHERE THE HELIX TURNS
shots.note: EVERY SLAB IS CARRIED BY TWO BRACKETS INTO THE WALL

shots.name: T_spiral_over
shots.caption: INTO THE SHAFT FROM ABOVE
shots.note: THE CENTRAL COLUMN IS TOWER()'S - IT BLOCKS FIRE ACROSS THE SHAFT

shots.name: T_gantry_entry
shots.caption: GANTRY - 5 FLOORS, 15 M, THE TALLEST A TOWER MAY BE
shots.note: A FULL LANDING EVERY 3.0 M - TOWER()'S OWN FLOOR SPACING

shots.name: T_gantry_landing
shots.caption: ON THE THIRD LANDING, TWO STOREYS ABOVE THE DOOR
shots.note: SOMEWHERE TO STAND AND FIGHT AT FIVE DIFFERENT HEIGHTS

shots.name: T_gantry_over
shots.caption: INTO THE SHAFT FROM ABOVE
shots.note: THE ONLY TOWER WHERE THE TOP IS OUT OF SIGHT FROM THE BOTTOM
